title: Showcase: first talk to the family
summary: Give your first live talk to the family, then run this week's Sprout card with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part.

steps.title: Live in front of the family
steps.body:
This talk is live, not a recording alone in your room. Gather your family, stand up, and give a 60 second talk about something from this season, the same rules as always: speak to the back wall, one pause on purpose, look at one person per sentence.

After the talk, take two questions from the family. Answer each one out loud, no notes.

If a question stumps you, do not guess and do not go quiet. Say exactly what you do know, say what you are not sure of, and say how you would find out. That answer is worth as much as one you already knew.

steps.title: Teach someone younger
steps.body:
A parent card is the short card in the app that a grown-up normally uses with Sprout. It has a title, a list of three to five steps to do together, and two or three "things to notice" while you do them.

This week you are the one running it, not a grown-up. Open this week's Sprout parent card from Sprout's screen, and read it once, all the way through, before you start, so you know what is supposed to happen.

Then run the card with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part. Let them do the actual activity: the sorting, the counting, the pattern, whatever the card asks for. Your job is to read the prompts and notice what they do, not to do it for them.

Watch for one thing they do that surprises you, something they get right that you did not expect, or a way they solve it that is not how you would have.
checklist: I let them do it, I did not do it for them
I noticed one thing they could do that surprised me

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the live talk and the two questions afterward, phone propped up, whole face in frame.
